newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Former guerrillas in El Salvador deny Peru links.
newsitem.headline: Former guerrillas in El Salvador deny Peru links.

text.p: El Salvador's former guerrillas on Wednesday denied having trained the Peruvian rebels holding 74 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.

Peruvian police had claimed that two former guerrillas of El Salvador's Farabundo Marti National Liberation Front (FMLN) trained members of Peru's Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement, which stormed a gala at the Japanese ambassador's residence on Dec. 17 and took hundreds of people hostage.
The FMLN, once considered among the most professional guerrilla armies in the world, signed a peace treaty with the Salvadoran government five years ago and now is a legal political party.

"If in the case that it is proven that both these people belonged to the Front, we want to say categorically that the FMLN party is not responsible for these actions," FMLN Congressman Miguel Saenz told reporters.

The alleged Salvadoran guerrilla trainers were identified only by their code names Osmin and Roman. The allegation has become a political issue in El Salvador because of upcoming local and congressional elections on March 16.
